items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board 2020 Delhi Basic
items.stem: If the sum and product of the zeroes of a quadratic polynomial are 3 and −10 respectively, find the quadratic polynomial.
items.answer:
Sum of zeroes, α + β = 3 and product of zeroes, αβ = −10.
Quadratic polynomial p(x) = x² − (α + β)x + αβ = x² − 3x − 10.
items.concept: Sum and product of the zeroes
items.ocr: Printed solution line reads p(x) = x² − (α + β) + αβ; the missing factor x after (α + β) restored from the next line, which gives x² − 3x − 10.

items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board 2020 OD Basic
items.stem: If the sum of the zeroes of the quadratic polynomial kx² + 2x + 3k is equal to their product, then what is the value of k?
items.answer:
p(x) = kx² + 2x + 3k. Comparing with ax² + bx + c gives a = k, b = 2, c = 3k.
Sum of zeroes, α + β = −b/a = −2/k.
Product of zeroes, αβ = c/a = 3k/k = 3.
Given α + β = αβ, so −2/k = 3 ⇒ k = −2/3.
items.concept: Sum and product of the zeroes
items.ocr: MinerU wrote the comparison line as "Comparing it ) y ax² + bx + c"; read as "Comparing it with ax² + bx + c".

items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board 2020 Delhi Basic
items.stem: If α and β are the zeroes of the polynomial 2x² − 13x + 6, then what is the value of α + β?
items.answer:
p(x) = 2x² − 13x + 6. Comparing with ax² + bx + c gives a = 2, b = −13, c = 6.
Sum of zeroes α + β = −b/a = −(−13)/2 = 13/2.
items.concept: Sum and product of the zeroes

items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board 2020 OD Basic
items.stem: If one zero of the polynomial (3x² + 8x + k) is the reciprocal of the other, then what is the value of k?
items.answer:
Let the zeroes be α and 1/α.
Product of zeroes, α · (1/α) = constant term / coefficient of x²
1 = k/3 ⇒ k = 3.

items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-1 OD 2011
items.stem: What is the value of x, for which the polynomials x² − 1 and x² − 2x + 1 vanish simultaneously?
items.answer: x² − 1 = (x − 1)(x + 1) and x² − 2x + 1 = (x − 1)(x − 1). Both have 1 as a zero, so both vanish when x = 1.
items.concept: What a zero is

items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board 2010
items.stem: Find a quadratic polynomial whose zeroes are −3 and 4.
items.answer:
Here α = −3 and β = 4.
Sum of zeroes, α + β = −3 + 4 = 1
Product of zeroes, αβ = −3 × 4 = −12
So the quadratic polynomial is x² − (α + β)x + αβ = x² − x − 12.
items.concept: Sum and product of the zeroes

items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-1 OD 2013
items.stem: What is the lowest value of x² + 4x + 2?
items.answer:
x² + 4x + 2 = (x² + 4x + 4) − 2 = (x + 2)² − 2.
Here (x + 2)² is always non-negative and its lowest value is zero. Thus the lowest value of (x + 2)² − 2 is −2, attained when x + 2 = 0, i.e. x = −2.
items.concept: General form of a quadratic

items.stem: If the sum of the zeroes of the polynomial f(x) = 2x³ − 3kx² + 4x − 5 is 6, then what is the value of k?
items.answer: Sum of the zeroes = 3k/2, so 6 = 3k/2 ⇒ k = 12/3 = 4.

items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-1 2010
items.stem: Calculate the zeroes of the polynomial p(x) = 4x² − 12x + 9.
items.answer:
p(x) = 4x² − 12x + 9
= 4x² − 6x − 6x + 9
= 2x(2x − 3) − 3(2x − 3)
= (2x − 3)(2x − 3)
Substituting p(x) = 0 and solving we get x = 3/2, 3/2.
Hence the zeroes of the polynomial are 3/2 and 3/2.
items.concept: Splitting the middle term
items.ocr: Repeated OCR echo "x = 32, 32" after the fractions removed; the values are 3/2, 3/2.

items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board 2009
items.stem: If the sum of the zeroes of the quadratic polynomial 3x² − kx + 6 is 3, then find the value of k.
items.answer:
Sum of the zeroes = −(coefficient of x)/(coefficient of x²).
3 = −(−k)/3 ⇒ k = 9.
items.concept: Sum and product of the zeroes

items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-1 Foreign 2015
items.stem: If −1 is a zero of the polynomial f(x) = x² − 7x − 8, then calculate the other zero.
items.answer:
f(x) = x² − 7x − 8. Let the other zero be k.
Sum of zeroes, −1 + k = −(−7/1) = 7 ⇒ k = 8.
Hence the other zero is 8.
items.concept: What a zero is

items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-1 2016
items.stem: If zeroes of the polynomial x² + 4x + 2a are a and 2/a, then find the value of a.
items.answer:
Product of zeroes, c/a = 2a/1 = a × (2/a) = 2.
2a = 2 ⇒ a = 1.
items.concept: Sum and product of the zeroes

items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-1 2013
items.stem: Find all the zeroes of f(x) = x² − 2x.
items.answer:
f(x) = x² − 2x = x(x − 2).
Substituting f(x) = 0 and solving we get x = 0, 2.
Hence the zeroes are 0 and 2.
items.concept: What a zero is

items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-1 2012
items.stem: Find the condition that zeroes of polynomial p(x) = ax² + bx + c are reciprocal of each other.
items.answer:
Let α and 1/α be the zeroes of p(x).
Product of zeroes, c/a = α × (1/α) = 1, so c/a = 1.
Hence the required condition is c = a.
items.concept: Sum and product of the zeroes

items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-1 2013
items.stem: Find the values of a and b, if they are the zeroes of polynomial x² + ax + b.
items.answer:
p(x) = x² + ax + b, with a and b as its zeroes.
Product of zeroes: ab = b ⇒ a = 1.
Sum of zeroes: a + b = −a ⇒ b = −2a = −2.
Hence a = 1 and b = −2.
items.concept: Sum and product of the zeroes

items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board 2020 OD Standard
items.stem: What are the zeroes of the polynomial x² − 3x − m(m + 3)?
items.answer:
p(x) = x² − 3x − m(m + 3).
Substituting x = −m: p(−m) = (−m)² − 3(−m) − m(m + 3) = m² + 3m − m² − 3m = 0, so x = −m is a zero.
Substituting x = m + 3: p(m + 3) = (m + 3)² − 3(m + 3) − m(m + 3) = (m + 3)[m + 3 − 3 − m] = (m + 3)(0) = 0, so x = m + 3 is also a zero.
Hence the zeroes are −m and m + 3.
items.concept: What a zero is
